title: Malaysia & Singapore, from the Malay and Chinese press

stories.text: The court allowed Perikatan Nasional to suspend the Registrar of Societies' move to cancel the party's registration.
Civil servants who use Waze face immediate disciplinary action.
Nearly 7.7 million Waze user records are allegedly being sold on the dark web.
Loke said Zetrix AI has not yet paid RM314 million in arrears from government revenue collection.
Two former senior Tabung Haji officers were charged with cheating over RM3.3 billion in hibah payments.
Malaysia will demand that Indonesia take effective action on the haze.
Schools in Selangor, Melaka and Pahang will operate as usual tomorrow despite the haze.
Mustapha said the Madani government has resolved 12 of the 16 matters under MA63.
Melaka election: PN has not finalised seat allocation with BN.
Nine members of the 'Geng Yunaa' syndicate, said to earn RM5.4 million a year from prostitution, will be charged tomorrow.
Singapore's PSI is expected to return to unhealthy levels tomorrow; NEA says conditions may improve on Sunday.
Singaporeans aged 60 and above can get free N95 masks from 23 October.
A baby boy who was abused to death had not been referred to MSF; authorities appointed an independent panel to strengthen child protection.
In Singapore, the re-employment rate within six months for workers retrenched in their 50s fell to 41.9%.
Singapore is allocating an extra $135 million for coastal protection and flood resilience.
